title: Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains greenstone belt and early life traces
summary: The Barberton Greenstone Belt in northeastern South Africa preserves volcanic and sedimentary rocks about 3.6 to 3.25 billion years old, among the best-preserved of that age. Its Moodies Group sandstones, about 3.22 billion years old, hold carbon-rich laminae interpreted as microbial mats, giving a rare view of early coastal ecosystems. UNESCO listed the area in 2018.

uncertainty.note: Range runs from the oldest rocks UNESCO describes (3.6 Ga) to the Moodies Group microbial mats (ca. 3.22 Ga). Sources give no error bars in the passages read.

as_recorded.value: 3.6 to 3.25 billion years (volcanic and sedimentary rocks)

where.modern_name: Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains, Mpumalanga, South Africa
where.historical_name: No polity; Archaean greenstone belt on the eastern Kaapvaal Craton

paleo.not_applicable: Age of 3.6–3.22 Ga is beyond the 1000 Ma limit of the GPlates plate models.

importance.justification: One of the oldest well-preserved volcanic and sedimentary successions on Earth, with mats among the oldest mappable biofacies in shallow-water siliciclastic settings.

sources.title: Composition and microfacies of Archean microbial mats (Moodies Group, ca. 3.22 Ga, South Africa)

sources.author: Antonia Gamper, Christoph Heubeck, Dieter Demske, Marek Hoehse

reviewer_note: Least sure of the "early life" reading: biogenicity of the Moodies laminae is an interpretation (Gamper et al. say "suggest"); the 3.5 Ga in the id is a midpoint, not a measured age.
